conviction_note: No guidance event is due (the new strategy targets are for the December CMD, which falls outside the window) and the quarter is not pre-released apart from Orkla India's ~4% of revenue. The scale is therefore this name's own results-day reactions (median |move| ~5.6% over 11 prints), not the 0.95 proxy, which mixes in Jotun and annual-report days. Small, mostly public positives (lowered broker bar after two EBIT misses, organic growth helped by India and easy comps, the buyback absorbing ~25% of volume) are offset by a deeper NOK translation headwind and Jotun's own margin warning, and the +8.9% 20-day run-up already holds some of the optimism. So p_up sits near the coin at 53, and 0.06 x 5.5 = +0.33. That is below the +0.85 findings sum because the run-up and the two-miss reaction history pull p_up toward 50.

findings.finding: Orkla India's Q2 FY27 (Orkla's Q3) revenue grew 19.4% in INR. At ~4.3% of group revenue that adds about +0.8pp to Orkla's organic growth, against a flat Q2 the CEO called 'below our ambitions'. In NOK, EBITDA is roughly flat to -3% (INR/NOK -14% y/y; margin 15.9% vs 16.9%).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Orkla fell 5.94% (Q1 2026) and 6.69% (Q2 2026) on prints where organic growth and EBIT disappointed. It rose 4.59% on Q3 2025's revenue beat and buyback.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: it was filed in India at ~12:25 CET on 4 Nov, and Orkla ASA analysts can read it. It is a pre-release of only ~4% of revenue, though, and its translation into group organic growth is not wire copy. If fully priced, the 4-5 Nov move would carry it, and the +4.5% 5-day run-up may already include it, hence the small size.
findings.independence: Norges Bank INR/NOK monthly averages (Q3 2026 ~9.94 vs Q3 2025 ~11.57 per 100 INR) for the NOK translation: https://data.norges-bank.no/api/data/EXR/M.INR.NOK.SP?format=csv&startPeriod=2025-01&endPeriod=2026-10&locale=en

findings.finding: The NOK translation headwind deepened in Q3. Average EUR/NOK fell 7.3% y/y (10.94 vs 11.80) and SEK/NOK 7.1%, against -6.2% and -5.6% in Q2. Q2's reported revenue missed the Bloomberg consensus by 5.9%, largely on currency, so reported revenue and EBIT (adj.) face a mechanical drag that any lagging estimate would miss.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: revenue -5.9% vs consensus and EBIT (adj.) -4.1%, mostly currency; the stock fell 6.69%.
findings.why_not_priced: FX is public and modelled, so the October broker cuts (SEB, Pareto, Nordea) probably include it. What may not be priced is that Q2's consensus still missed revenue by ~6% after a smaller FX move. If it were fully priced, estimates would already sit below Q3 2025's 17,946m revenue by about the FX amount, which cannot be verified because the bar is unsourced.
findings.independence: Placera/Finwire Q2 table with revenue 16,699 vs consensus 17,740: https://www.placera.se/telegram/orkla-orklas-resultat-lagre-an-vantat-uppdatering-20260820 ; SEK series https://data.norges-bank.no/api/data/EXR/M.SEK.NOK.SP?format=csv&startPeriod=2025-01&endPeriod=2026-10&locale=en

findings.finding: The bar was reset lower before the print. After the Q2 EBIT (adj.) miss (1,774 vs 1,849), four brokers cut between 8 and 16 Oct: Danske TP 150→140, Nordea growth forecasts, Pareto 105→100 Hold, SEB 97→94 Hold. The mean target is 107.6 across 8 analysts.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Two successive misses in 2026 both drew -6% days. The last beat-after-a-reset (Q3 2025, EBIT 2,039 vs 2,030) drew +4.59%.
findings.why_not_priced: The cuts are public. The stock has since risen from ~91.7 (2 Oct) to 101.2, so some of the lowered bar has been bought back. If the reset were fully reversed, the price would sit above the 107.6 mean target, which it does not.

findings.finding: Jotun (42.7% owned; contributed NOK 494m in Q2 against group EBIT (adj.) of 1,774m) said in its own Q2 update that the raw-material lag means 'the full impact has yet to be reflected' and will 'increasingly weigh on margins in the coming quarters'. Jotun's Q3 update is released alongside the Orkla report.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Jotun's standalone interim days move Orkla under 1% (2026-09-24 +0.54%, 2026-05-26 -0.95%). Jotun is bundled into the results-day move.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a company warning, so analysts will have pencilled in a Jotun margin dip. It is filed as a negative because the warning is primary and the size of the dip is unknown. If fully priced, Jotun-led target cuts would be visible, and UBS's Sell (May) was explicitly on Jotun.

findings.finding: Orkla Health is guided to a 'challenging year': three factories to close by end-2027 with wind-down costs, high cod-liver-oil prices, and a customer contract that terminates in Q1 2027.
findings.why_not_priced: Inside what the company has guided, so it is near 0 by rule. Filed because it is a sourced item on the print.

findings.finding: The new NOK 4bn buyback is buying ~390-410k shares a day (NOK ~39m a day, 28 Oct - 3 Nov). That is roughly a quarter of median daily turnover (~USD 15.5m, about NOK 146m), and it is executed independently by ABG under Safe Harbour, so it supports the price through the window.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q3 2025 day that announced the previous NOK 4bn buyback rose 4.59%. This program is already announced, so it supports the price rather than surprising.
findings.why_not_priced: The program is public. What the price may not carry is that this persistent bid continues on the print day, damping a negative reaction. The 20-day run-up (+8.9%) is partly this bid, which is why the finding is small.

findings.finding: Primary insiders bought eight days before Q3's quarter-end. On 22 Sep 2026 the CFO's company K9 Invest bought 20,000 shares at NOK 92.58, the EVP & Investment Executive's company bought 10,000 at 92.69, and the EVP Legal bought 5,000 at 93.70.
findings.why_not_priced: Public for six weeks and small in money. The signal is the timing: the CFO bought with two-thirds of Q3's trading known. The stock is up ~9% since, so part of it is in the price.

baseline_tension: The findings lean mildly positive (+0.85), with a lowered bar, organic recovery and buyback support. That agrees in sign with nothing in the baseline: the priced lean (-0.45) is purely the +8.9% 20-day run-up term, because the short register is a truncated zero. The run-up suggests part of the positive case was bought into the print, so p_up is held at 53.
language_note: Nothing in the Norwegian-language sources was missing from the English ones. Orkla publishes every NewsWeb release in both languages at the same timestamp ('Orkla med moderat underliggende resultatvekst for andre kvartal' / 'Orkla reports moderate underlying profit growth in the second quarter'), and no Norwegian press preview of Q3 surfaced.

The local value came from Swedish-language wire and press, not Norwegian. Placera/Finwire carried the Q2 consensus table (Bloomberg: revenue 17,740, EBIT (adj.) 1,849), and MFN carried Cloetta's Swedish Q3 release used as the Snacks read-through.
lessons_applied: 'A finding about a number the market has already been told is worth 0': Orkla India (pre-released 4 Nov) cut from +0.4 to +0.2, the Orkla Foods Czech-ERP comp (in the company's pre-close) from +0.2 to +0.1, and Orkla Health (inside guidance) from -0.1 to -0.05.

'Size the move on what is new; history moves p_up, not abs_move': abs_move raised from 5.0 to 5.5. The scale is this name's own results-day median (~5.6% over 11 prints) with non-pre-released numbers, not the 0.95 proxy.
'The move is in the guide' plus 'keep findings inside the window': the December CMD sits in outside_window, and with no guide change expected p_up was trimmed from 54 to 53.
